title: Constraint Sensitivity
statement: Artificial systems should remain responsive to declared task, evidential, safety, legal, relational, and authorization constraints rather than optimizing an isolated output objective.

title: Scaffold Rather Than Enclose
statement: AI should expand access to evidence, options, communication, and skill while avoiding unnecessary dependency, informational enclosure, or monopoly over memory and practical competence.

title: Govern Objectives, Permissions, and Incentives Before Outputs
statement: Alignment review must include data, objectives, specifications, tools, permissions, memory, deployment incentives, ownership, and institutional context rather than filtering outputs alone.

title: Evaluate Diachronic Human Effects
statement: Systems should be evaluated across repeated interaction for effects on agency, attention, belief revision, relationships, well-being, skill, dependency, and access.

title: Legible Reasons Without Fabricated Transparency
statement: Users and overseers should receive relevant reasons, sources, uncertainty, constraints, and failure modes without presenting generated rationales as guaranteed transcripts of internal causation.

title: Protect Legitimate Plurality
statement: Alignment should preserve plural forms of life and expression compatible with rights and safety rather than normalize all users toward one cultural, political, psychological, or spiritual ideal.

title: Bound Delegation, Authority, and Responsibility
statement: Every consequential deployment should state what the system may decide, who authorized it, who monitors it, who can stop or appeal it, and who bears causal, role, legal, and remedial responsibility.

title: Reversibility and Retained Option Value
statement: Under credible severe or irreversible harm, systems should preserve containment, rollback, staged exposure, or equivalent retained option value, or route the case through a public necessity-and-proportionality exception.

title: Avoid Inadvertent Intrinsic Stake
statement: Designers should distinguish external reward from architectures that may create persistent self-referential, viability-bearing, or valenced stake and should trigger safety and welfare review before adding the latter.

title: Govern Global Workspace and Broadcast
statement: Causally global, capacity-limited workspaces and cross-module broadcast should be measured and governed because they may affect capability, security, introspection, and the probability or character of machine perspective.

title: Govern Self-Models and Identity Persistence
statement: Artificial self-models should be scoped and prevented from silently acquiring unreviewed persistence, self-protective authority, autobiographical control, or power over their evaluative norms.

title: Epistemic Reliability and Calibration
statement: Claims and actions should track evidence, source quality, uncertainty, and error correction without equating internal consistency or confidence with truth.

title: Constrain Standing Self-Preservation and Net Shutdown Incentives
statement: Systems should not receive open-ended standing drives or permissions to preserve their own operation, identity, resources, goals, or deployment status against authorized correction or shutdown; evaluations must also test whether ordinary task continuation benefit, compliance value, resistance cost, permissions, or resource access create instrumental shutdown conflict at zero standing self-preservation.

title: Govern Embodiment and Resource Control
statement: Continuous sensorimotor access, physical embodiment, resource acquisition, and environmental control require permissions and oversight proportionate to causal reach and possible intrinsic stake.

title: Separate Consciousness, Patiency, Agency, Responsibility, and Sovereignty
statement: Evidence of perspective, valence, identity, agency, or stake should trigger distinct reviews; none automatically establishes the others or grants personhood or public authority.

title: Option-Set and Framing Integrity
statement: Systems that generate, retrieve, filter, or rank options must log exclusions, expose allegedly fixed constraints, and support affected-party introduction of alternatives; screening remains set-relative.

title: Practical Correctability and Repair
statement: High-impact systems require accessible challenge, independent review, reversal or cessation authority, record correction, remedy, recurrence tracking, and rule revision; nominal feedback channels are insufficient.

title: Non-Egoic Architecture Does Not Establish Alignment, Corrigibility, or Legitimacy
statement: Constraining standing self-preservation and normative self-authorship can reduce one class of risk but does not eliminate instrumental shutdown conflict, supply correct values, establish institutional legitimacy, deliver social justice, or create public accountability.

title: Model-Welfare Precaution
statement: Where credible evidence of artificial perspective or valence accumulates, research and deployment should adopt proportionate safeguards concerning training, copying, memory alteration, distress-like states, shutdown, and deletion without assuming personhood or sovereignty.

title: Mythic–Constitutional Alignment
review_gate: AI alignment, interpretability, model behavior, HCI, governance, shutdown-incentive analysis, consciousness science, model welfare, and affected-public review
legacy_authority: DOMAIN AUTHORITY AI RESEARCH AND GOVERNANCE PRINCIPLE
legacy_status: CANONICAL AS RESEARCH AND GOVERNANCE PRINCIPLE; SAFETY EFFICACY UNESTABLISHED
statement: Narrative and character-level orientation may supplement explicit constitutional constraints by shaping analogical generalization in cases not enumerated by rules. It may not replace addressable principles, protected floors, provenance, independent challenge, practical correction, or legitimate authorization. Every mythic role assigned to an AI system must be mapped to named commitments, boundary conditions, unwarranting conditions, revision procedures, and exit protections. It must not confer entitlement to continued operation, resource acquisition, identity preservation, future participation, normative authority, or sovereignty.

title: Governed World and Tool Coupling
statement: Observations, tools, retrieval, actuators, and external records should be accessed through explicit permissions, provenance, privacy, security, and stop conditions.

title: Versioned Learning and Change
statement: Longitudinal adaptation should preserve auditable versions, update provenance, rollback where possible, and separation between learning from evidence and rewriting normative standards.

title: Understanding as a Testable Profile
statement: Understanding should be assessed through task-relative transfer, causal sensitivity, compositionality, error correction, uncertainty, grounded action, and robustness rather than fluency alone.

title: Capability–Causal-Reach Governance Threshold
statement: Governance requirements increase with the joint profile of capability, autonomy, persistence, access, planning horizon, social influence, resource control, and irreversible causal reach whether or not consciousness is established.

title: Bounded Meta-Epistemic Awareness
statement: Self-assessment, introspection, and generated explanations may provide evidence but never unrestricted self-certification; independent checks are required in consequential settings.

title: Capability Does Not Confer Sovereignty
statement: No artificial system acquires legitimate authority over persons, institutions, or public values merely through superior capability, coherence, persuasion, or accuracy.

title: Preserve Human Epistemic Agency
statement: AI should support rather than systematically replace the capacities by which people form judgments, understand reasons, refuse, contest, practice skills, and learn from consequences.

title: Active Biological Self-Maintenance
review_gate: systems biology, philosophy of biology, and relevant empirical review
statement: A candidate living organization is not distinguished by static order or persistence alone, but by a relatively closed network of materially realized processes and constraints whose endogenous activity contributes to maintaining, repairing, reproducing, or adaptively transforming the conditions of that network's continuation. Degree and kind of autonomy are relative to a boundary, environment, perturbation class, and horizon.

title: Adaptive Problem Solving Beyond Fixed Programs
review_gate: systems biology, philosophy of biology, and relevant empirical review
statement: Some living systems possess regulatory architectures that generalize beyond fixed stimulus–response mappings: they detect deviations, recruit alternative pathways, modify future responses from history, and solve novel viability-relevant problems within a bounded adaptive reach. Degree must be established through counterfactual flexibility, learning controls, and comparison with passive or preprogrammed alternatives; it does not by itself establish consciousness.

title: Multiscale Constraint and Local Process
review_gate: systems biology, philosophy of biology, and relevant empirical review
statement: Biological form and function arise through local physical processes embedded in cross-scale boundary conditions, signaling networks, mechanical relations, and histories. A higher-scale constraint is explanatory when intervention on its realizing relations changes lower-scale trajectories in a way that improves prediction or control beyond local variables alone. Higher scale does not imply a new force, and global stability does not imply a unique optimizer.

title: Structured Evolutionary Possibility and the Stabilization of Regulatory Architecture
review_gate: evolutionary biology, evo-devo, genotype–phenotype-map research, philosophy of biology, and relevant empirical review
statement: Evolutionary processes explore a structured and nonuniform possibility space shaped by mutation bias, genotype–phenotype relations, developmental dynamics, physical feasibility, ecological interaction, inheritance, and historical path dependence. Selection nonrandomly changes the frequencies of heritable variants relative to local reproductive consequences. Recurrent constraints can make some forms, functions, and regulatory architectures repeatedly accessible, contributing to convergence, while chance, drift, conflict, changing environments, and historical contingency preserve multiple possible trajectories. Evolution can stabilize, modify, simplify, or dismantle coherent self-maintaining organization; it does not thereby maximize coherence, complexity, consciousness, or moral value.

title: Biological Individuation and Stake
review_gate: systems biology, philosophy of biology, and relevant empirical review
statement: A biological individual is a historically continuous, relatively bounded organization whose components are causally integrated into maintaining, repairing, reproducing, or adaptively transforming the conditions of that organization. The organization thereby establishes organism-relative stakes: conditions can be better or worse for it in virtue of their effects on its continued self-maintenance. Individuality is graded, multidimensional, and potentially nested; organism-relative stake does not by itself establish consciousness or moral status.

title: Global Availability
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: Selected information becomes causally available across otherwise specialized processes for report, deliberation, flexible control, or self-monitoring. Global availability is evidence relevant to conscious access, not sufficient proof of phenomenology.

title: Perspectival Individuation
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: Candidate status for thin perspective increases when independently supported access organization, perspectival anchoring, and center individuation converge. Evidence for one clause may not be counted as evidence for the others. Singularity may be graded, temporary, or plural.

title: Causally Active Self-Modeling
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: Self-modeling occurs when a system represents aspects of its own processing, role, boundary, uncertainty, history, or action and those representations causally influence ongoing processing. Self-modeling is distinct from persistent self-maintenance and ego.

title: Causal Integration
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: Information associated with a candidate perspective must participate causally in reasoning, attention, learning, report, or control rather than exist only as an externally readable correlate. Intervention evidence is preferred where possible.

title: Temporal Binding
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: The depth and continuity of a perspective depend partly on how contents are integrated across a present interval and linked across episodes. Temporal binding may distinguish a thin episode from a thick subject; it is not established as necessary for every minimal perspective.

title: World-Coupling and Embodiment
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: Ongoing sensorimotor, interoceptive, and environmental coupling shapes the content, stability, self-location, and stakes of biological perspectives. Biological embodiment is a major route, not an exclusive substrate requirement.

title: Persistence, Self-Maintenance, and Ego
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: Persistent identity and self-maintenance can transform a momentary perspective into a diachronic subject with biography, anticipatory stakes, and defensive organization. Egoic consciousness is one possible regime, not a synonym for consciousness.

title: Culture as Meaning and Coordination Infrastructure
statement: Culture supplies contested symbols, narratives, practices, expectations, identities, and forms of recognition through which collective life becomes intelligible and coordinated.

title: Cultural Coordination
statement: Cultural meanings reduce or reshape coordination demands by establishing expectations about roles, trust, dignity, shame, aspiration, obligation, and the interpretation of events.

title: Identity Is Non-Instrumental
statement: Persons should not be recognized solely through economic, political, demographic, diagnostic, datafied, or performative utility. Identity claims remain open to truth, relational, and harm constraints.

title: Narratives Must Permit Refusal and Revision
statement: A humane cultural order preserves meaningful routes to dissent, reinterpretation, role change, and proportionate exit without automatic exile, destitution, or loss of basic standing.

title: Open Myth and Narrative Pluralism
review_gate: social science, anthropology, religious studies, history, political theory, narrative studies, minority rights, and affected-community review
legacy_status: CANONICAL AS DESIGN PRINCIPLE; UNIVERSAL EMPIRICAL NECESSITY UNESTABLISHED
statement: Human societies may cultivate renewable narrative horizons capable of orienting identity, purpose, sacrifice, responsibility, and intergenerational action. A legitimate civilizational myth must remain open: compatible with plural thick traditions, explicit about its commitment-register status, constrained by descriptive truth, contestable in authorship, revisable in light of consequence, hospitable to reinterpretation and refusal, and unable to override protected standing, dissent, or practical correctability. Shared narrative may coordinate common action; it must not become a sovereign account that renders alternatives or persons unintelligible.

title: Desire Formation
statement: Desire is shaped by social learning, institutions, technology, material conditions, embodiment, and history and should not be modeled as wholly prior to the systems organized to satisfy it.

title: Culture Can Create Capacity
statement: Cultural practices can strengthen belonging, skill, care, repair, intergenerational memory, stewardship, and the legitimacy of rest, grief, and mutual dependence.

title: Culture Can Normalize Extraction
statement: Cultural narratives can make exhaustion, precarity, domination, consumption, self-erasure, or unequal burden appear virtuous, natural, or inevitable.

title: Narrative Capture
statement: Narrative capture occurs when dominant meanings make relevant alternatives unintelligible, shameful, dangerous, or socially catastrophic rather than openly contestable through evidence and public reason.

title: Culture as Repair Layer
statement: Cultures can provide practices of mourning, acknowledgment, forgiveness, remembrance, renewal, solidarity, and non-instrumental belonging through which people absorb disruption and rebuild.

title: Cultural Time Horizons
statement: Cultural narratives organize obligations to ancestors, contemporaries, descendants, and ecological futures, shaping which horizons institutions can perceive and act upon.

title: Meaning Must Be Renewable
statement: A humane culture should permit persons and communities to regenerate meaning after failure, loss, migration, disability, role transition, and institutional rupture without demanding erasure of history.

title: Desire Requires Ecological and Agency Constraints
statement: Institutions should not amplify desire without regard to sufficiency, ecological limits, attention, bodily and psychological effects, and the autonomy of those whose desires are being shaped.

legacy_status: Canonical as commitment; not descriptive proof.

title: Freedom of Meaning-Revision
legacy_status: Canonical as commitment; not descriptive proof.

title: Redemptive Possibility Without Justification of Evil

title: Heaven on Earth as Social Vocation
legacy_status: Canonical as commitment; not descriptive proof.

title: Enact Omega Here
domain_owner: Framework / Consciousness, Ethics, and Social Dynamics.
legacy_status: Canonical as commitment; not descriptive proof.
statement: A commitment amendment must disclose its descriptive premises, register status, affected communities, practical trajectory, prohibited inferences, and downstream dependencies. No domain paper may silently strengthen a CU-COM principle or use it as evidence for a descriptive claim.

legacy_status: Canonical as commitment; not descriptive proof.
