title: Domain-Specified Constrained Dynamics
statement: A domain dynamics specifies how states or trajectories change under declared constraints, couplings, interventions, and environmental conditions. Its general form may be written \[ \mathcal F_{\mathcal D}[x,\dot x,\ddot x,\ldots;K,G,E,u,t]=0, \] or as a transition kernel, update relation, control system, or path measure appropriate to the domain. There is no currently established universal equation of the form \[ \frac{dC}{dt} = \alpha\nabla C\cdot v - \beta\frac{dS}{dt} + \gamma\Lambda \] governing every physical, biological, psychological, social, and artificial system.

title: Memory as History-Conditioned Constraint
statement: Memory is any history-dependent modification through which prior states or events alter the system's present dynamics, accessible representations, or space of future continuations. A general representation is \[ K_t=\mathcal U(K_{t-1},x_{t-1},a_{t-1},E_{t-1}), \] or \[ \dot x_t=F(x_t;H_{0:t}), \] where the relevant history may be compressed into state variables or remain irreducibly path-dependent for the model.

title: Regulated Coherence-Seeking
statement: Systems with feedback, error sensitivity, and persistence-bearing constraints may exhibit regulated tendencies that restore or expand domain-specific coherence after perturbation.

title: Gateway to Active Biological Self-Maintenance
statement: The transition from passive physical persistence to active biological self-maintenance is owned by CU Biology. CU-D3 does not state an independent universal dynamics law.

title: Coherence Gradients Are Model-Relative
statement: A coherence gradient is defined only when a declared scalar \(C_{\mathcal D}\) of a type licensed under CU-FP2 and a geometry or inner product on the relevant state space have been specified: \[ \operatorname{grad}_{g} C_{\mathcal D} \quad\text{such that}\quad g(\operatorname{grad}_{g}C_{\mathcal D},v)=dC_{\mathcal D}[v]. \]

title: Non-Equilibrium Maintenance
statement: Many organized systems persist away from equilibrium only through ongoing exchange of energy, matter, information, or work with an environment. Their maintenance must be evaluated in the enlarged system that includes relevant costs and fluxes.

title: Multi-Timescale Organization
statement: Coherent trajectories may require coordination among processes operating at different characteristic timescales. Fast adaptation can destabilize slower identity or governance constraints; slow adaptation can fail in a rapidly changing environment.

title: Novelty Through Constrained Exploration
statement: Novel organization can arise when a system explores variable configurations while constraints preserve, select, or amplify some continuations. Exploration and constraint jointly shape innovation.

title: Repair Before Unbounded Optimization
legacy_status: CANONICAL as a design and normative bridge principle
statement: Where a system has protected viability, agency, or integrity conditions, maintaining repair capacity and restoring breached floors take priority over unbounded optimization of a secondary objective.

title: Multi-Scale Failure and Externalization
statement: A system may preserve apparent local coherence by transferring contradiction, risk, entropy, labor, trauma, or ecological cost to another scale, population, subsystem, or future. Such externalization must be included in any global evaluation.

title: The Justificatory Integrity Constraint
statement: An action, policy, or institution lacks adequate moral justification when its defense requires systematic distortion of relevant facts, reasons, affected parties, alternatives, or standards in order to protect a dominant identity, advantage, authority, or prior commitment. Integrity is necessary but not sufficient for permissibility.

title: Political Legitimacy and Public Justification
statement: Coercive or high-impact power is legitimate only to the degree that it is publicly answerable to those subject to it, preserves protected standing, remains contestable, discloses evidence and uncertainty, and includes practical correction and remedy.

title: Rights as Protected Conditions of Agency and Patiency
statement: Rights protect bodily and psychological integrity, welfare, liberty, capability, participation, and standing against domination and unrestricted aggregate tradeoff. Their content requires independent moral, legal, historical, and democratic argument.

title: Democracy as a Conditional Corrective Achievement
statement: Democratic forms are valuable when they distribute political agency, preserve opposition and minority standing, constrain power, and enable peaceful correction. Majority rule or actual consensus alone is insufficient.

title: Constraint on Political Means
statement: Political ends do not justify means that destroy the truth conditions, protected standing, accountability, or corrective institutions required to pursue, evaluate, and revise those ends.

title: Responsibility–Authority Alignment
statement: Responsibility should be assigned with attention to causal contribution, knowledge, control, authority, benefit, coercion, prevention capacity, and repair capacity. Institutions should neither impose responsibility without adequate authority nor permit authority without accountability.

title: Affected-Community Participation
statement: People governed, classified, burdened, or represented by an ethical principle must have substantive, accessible, and appropriately authoritative participation in its development, application, and review. Participation supplements rather than replaces evidence and argument. Promotion requires closure of every assigned review gate; unresolved conflict preserves provisional status and public dissent.

title: Moral Uncertainty, Precaution, and Reversibility
statement: Under credible risk of severe or irreversible harm, uncertainty should alter action in proportion to severity, plausibility, alternatives, reversibility, and the harms of delay. The application must either declare a context-appropriate reversibility, containment, rollback, staged-exposure, or retained-option floor, or publicly justify a necessity-and-proportionality exception. Uncertainty neither automatically permits exposure nor requires paralysis.

title: Moral Patiency Is Not Sovereignty
statement: Evidence that a being can experience welfare or suffering can ground protection without establishing responsibility, authority, or legitimate control over others.
disposition: Historical or domain alias; controlling identifier is CU-G6.

title: Compassionate Moral Address
statement: Accountability should preserve the standing of persons wherever protection allows, distinguish judgment from humiliation, and seek understanding sufficient for prevention and repair without converting compassion into excuse.

title: Agency, Patiency, and Degrees of Responsibility
statement: Moral patiency, moral agency, responsibility, and sovereignty are distinct. Responsibility varies with understanding, reason-responsiveness, control, authorship, coercion, and capacity for repair; diminished agency can reduce blame while increasing duties of protection.

title: Recognition and Affected-Being Standing
statement: Ethical evaluation must represent all materially affected beings according to relevant welfare, agency, vulnerability, relationship, history, and stake rather than treating absence of institutional voice as absence of a claim.

title: Diachronic and Beneficiary Responsibility
statement: Moral evaluation includes delayed, cumulative, intergenerational, and path-dependent consequences, together with responsibilities created by prior action, inherited advantage, ongoing benefit, and present capacity to prevent or repair harm.

title: Self-Deception as Moral Failure
statement: Motivated distortion becomes morally significant when it conceals avoidable harm, excludes affected beings, corrupts standards, blocks correction, diffuses responsibility, or protects power from accountability. Disagreement or error alone does not establish self-deception.

title: Protection, Accountability, and Repair
statement: Responses to wrongdoing should prioritize cessation and protection, truthful acknowledgment, proportionate accountability, restitution or reparation, restoration of standing, and prevention of recurrence. Punishment requires separate justification and is neither intrinsically reparative nor categorically excluded.

title: Moral Injury
domain_owner: Ethics with Psychology and clinical disciplines
statement: Moral injury names enduring psychological, social, relational, existential, or spiritual suffering associated with perpetrating, witnessing, failing to prevent, suffering, or being betrayed by morally significant wrong. Its descriptive use remains governed by the developing empirical literature.

title: Structural Moral Injury and Institutional Betrayal
domain_owner: Ethics with Psychology and Social Dynamics
statement: Institutions can produce or intensify moral injury when they impose morally compromising roles, deny adequate authority or alternatives, conceal harm, betray dependence, punish disclosure, or individualize structurally generated distress.

title: Local–Global Compatibility and Noncompensation
statement: Claims of collective benefit are inadequate when they depend on avoidable destruction of protected standing, agency, or welfare, or on hidden transfer of severe, nonconsensual, concentrated, or irreparable burdens. Sacrifice requires necessity, proportionality, distributional analysis, and repair.

title: Economic Evaluation Beyond Exchange Value
statement: Economic arrangements should be evaluated by their effects on material security, health, capability, agency, care, relationship, ecological viability, distribution, and repair as well as exchange value, output, and growth.

title: Capacity-Creating Activity
statement: Economic activity creates socially relevant value when it expands or sustains capabilities and conditions of viable life without imposing hidden, nonconsensual, severe, or unrepairable costs elsewhere.

title: Attention Is a Protected Scarce Capacity
statement: Human attention is limited, developmentally and politically consequential, and vulnerable to capture. Systems that profit by degrading autonomous attention, deliberation, or rest require explicit governance and affected-user evidence.

title: Human Agency Is Not a Commodity
statement: Markets may price services and time but should not erase the standing of persons to refuse, contest, exit, organize, and preserve domains of life not governed solely by exchange value.

title: Extraction
statement: Extraction occurs when an actor or system captures benefit or control by transferring hidden, nonconsensual, severe, or difficult-to-repair costs to other persons, communities, future generations, or ecosystems.

title: Growth Is Instrumental
statement: Growth in output, revenue, productivity, consumption, or capital is neither intrinsically adequate nor inadequate. Its value depends on distribution, purpose, ecological limits, agency, resilience, and long-horizon effects.

title: Labor as Agency-Bearing Activity
statement: Labor involves persons whose time, bodies, attention, skills, relationships, identities, and exit options have non-instrumental significance. Work arrangements require voice, safety, fair burden, and repair analysis in addition to output.

title: Capital as Stored Claim and Capacity
statement: Capital can coordinate long-horizon investment and can concentrate control over resources, decisions, and risk. Its evaluation requires ownership, governance, externalization, liquidity, and repair analysis.

title: Markets as Bounded Coordination Mechanisms
statement: Markets can aggregate some distributed information and coordinate exchange within suitable legal, material, and institutional conditions. They do not price every value, generate legitimate constraints by themselves, or guarantee just distributions.

title: Repair Costs Must Be Counted
statement: Actors should not treat foreseeable costs of restoring damaged people, communities, institutions, infrastructure, or ecosystems as external to the activity that produced or benefited from the damage.

title: Benefit Carries Repair Obligation
statement: Those who capture substantial benefits from an activity bear proportionate obligations for preventable harms and for maintaining the social, ecological, and institutional conditions that make the activity possible.

title: Time Horizons Must Be Disclosed
statement: Economic evaluation must disclose time horizon, discounting, debt structure, future liabilities, irreversibility, and which generations' benefits and harms are counted.

title: Constraint-Sensitive Engagement
statement: The pre-propositional basis of knowing is discriminating responsiveness to constraint. Differences in the environment or system state must make reliable differences to regulation or action.

title: Situated Pattern and Proto-Representation
statement: Recurrent constraint-sensitive responses can stabilize into expectations, maps, dispositions, and implicit models that guide action across related situations.

title: World-Coupled Claims
statement: Truth-apt belief begins when a representation is used as a claim about how things are and is exposed to correction by what it represents.

title: Diachronic and Intersubjective Correction
statement: Knowledge becomes more reliable when claims can be revised through time and exposed to independent access, testimony, criticism, replication, and preserved memory.

title: Explicit Models and Formal Systems
statement: At the modeling level, assumptions, variables, measurements, scope conditions, and inference rules are made explicit. Empirical models answer to observation; formal systems answer to proof relative to axioms.

title: Epistemic Governance
statement: Epistemic governance regulates how claims, models, measurements, feedback, options, and explanations are sourced, translated, tested, revised, versioned, authorized, challenged, and used across levels and institutions.

title: Meta-Epistemic Awareness
statement: Mature inquiry represents the limits and distortion pressures of its own methods, incentives, identities, scales, option sets, access conditions, observation channels, and institutional dependencies.

title: Coherence Under Constraint
statement: Coherence is **integrated relational organization under specified constraints**. For any substantive domain \(\mathcal D\), a coherence assessment has the dependency form \[ C_{\mathcal D}=C_{\mathcal D}(x;K,G,\pi,T), \] where \(x\) is the state, trajectory, or organization; \(K\) the relevant constraints; \(G\) the relational or coupling structure; \(\pi\) the scale, partition, observation, or access map; and \(T\) the temporal horizon.

title: Gradation, Profiles, Typed Scalars, Direction, and Incomparability
statement: Coherence assessments may admit degrees, directions of change, thresholds, vector profiles, preorders, partial orderings, viable regions, Pareto frontiers, risk functionals, or trajectory properties, but none of these structures is assumed universally. A domain may use: - a measurement scalar for one declared construct; - a vector profile \(\mathbf C\); - a decision scalarization for one declared choice; - a risk functional over uncertain states or trajectories; - a preorder or partial order \(\preceq_C\); - a viable set \(V\); - a threshold family; - a Pareto frontier; - or a trajectory property. Scalars are local, typed, purpose-bound, and scope-limited. A measurement scalar requires an independently defended interpretation of what it measures. A decision scalarization is a rule for choosing under declared tradeoffs, not evidence that the dimensions possess one natural total ordering. A risk functional additionally encodes a treatment of uncertainty, tails, delay, and irreversibility. Protected conditions are screened before scoring. No scalar may compensate for a floor violation. Variation above a protected floor may enter post-screen comparison only when its measurement, comparability, authority, and decision relevance are independently justified; otherwise the coordinate remains lexicographic or outside scoring.

title: Generative Constraint
statement: Constraints do not merely remove possibilities. Under suitable organization, restricting a space of states or transitions can create stable relations, capacities, meanings, and forms of agency that would not otherwise exist.

title: Multi-Scale and Multi-Horizon Evaluation
statement: A coherence claim is relative to scale and horizon. Apparent improvement within one boundary is not a global improvement when it depends on unmodeled damage exported to another system, scale, population, or future.

title: Non-Reduction and Explicit Translation
statement: Cross-domain integration requires explicit translation rather than identity by vocabulary. A valid translation states the source construct, target construct, preserved relation, new target constraints, lost information, evidence, alternatives, and failure conditions.

title: The Accessibility–Entropy Relation
legacy_status: [Formal result] in the finite classical setting; [Bridge principle] elsewhere
statement: For a specified finite partition, block averaging preserves coarse block masses while erasing within-block distinctions. Under that operation, statistical differentiation from global uniformity weakly decreases and Shannon entropy weakly increases. The losses and gains have the same equality condition but are not generally equal quantities. Let \(u_N=(1/N,\ldots,1/N)\), define \(D_N(p)=\lVert p-u_N Vert_2^2\), let \(B_b\) be blocks of size \(m_b\), let \(q_b=\sum_{i\in B_b}p_i\), and, when \(q_b>0\), let \(r_i^{(b)}=p_i/q_b\) for \(i\in B_b\). Blocks with \(q_b=0\) contribute zero to the weighted KL sum. Define \[ [E_\pi(p)]_i=\frac{q_b}{m_b} \quad(i\in B_b). \] Then \[ D_N(p)-D_N(E_\pi p) = \sum_b\sum_{i\in B_b} \left(p_i-\frac{q_b}{m_b}\right)^2, \] and \[ S(E_\pi p)-S(p) = \sum_bq_b\, D_{\mathrm{KL}}(r^{(b)}\Vert u_{m_b}) \geq0. \]

title: Failure, Collapse, Adaptation, and Repair
statement: A domain-specific failure occurs when organization required by an explicitly declared criterion can no longer be maintained, adapted, or repaired within the relevant horizon and intervention class. CU distinguishes perturbation, degradation, drift, fragmentation, threshold crossing, collapse, compensation, accommodation, transformation, restitution, restoration of standing, non-recurrence, and repair.

title: Identity as Constraint-Preserved Continuity
statement: An identity criterion specifies which relations, capacities, histories, boundaries, or constraints must remain invariant—or remain connected by an admissible continuity path—for a system to count as the same system through change. A general form is \[ x_t\equiv_{K_I,H}x_{t'} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \\text{an admissible path preserves identity-relevant constraints }K_I \\text{ over history }H. \] There is no single identity criterion for physical objects, organisms, persons, institutions, artificial agents, or candidate subjects. Self-modeling, self-maintenance, egoic persistence, phenomenal perspective, moral patiency, responsibility, and sovereignty are distinct.

title: Identity-Relevant Constraint Set
statement: A claim that a system persists as the same system must identify a nontrivial set of relations, capacities, boundaries, commitments, or continuities whose loss would defeat that identity judgment.

title: Continuity Across Component Change
statement: Token identity may survive replacement of components when an admissible continuity process preserves the identity-relevant organization. The relevant process is domain-specific and must distinguish continuation, copying, branching, reconstruction, and replacement.

title: Historical Dependence
statement: An identity claim must state whether history is constitutive, merely causally relevant, compressed into the current state, or recoverable only through an explicit history functional. Similar present states need not have the same identity when their continuity histories differ.

title: Endogenous Maintenance
statement: Some robust identities are partly constituted by the system’s own participation in maintaining the conditions of its continuation. Endogenous maintenance is not required for every object or momentary perspective and must not be inferred from persistence alone.

title: Transformation and Termination Criteria
statement: An identity account must state which changes count as continued identity, transformation, branching, replacement, copying, suspension, or termination. The criteria may be purpose-relative, but the practical purpose and parties affected by the judgment must be disclosed.

title: Discovery, Construction, and Corrigibility
statement: Systems encounter constraints they do not invent, while constructing models, measures, categories, and practices through which those constraints become intelligible. Responsible inquiry distinguishes discovered resistance from constructed representation and remains corrigible when the representation fails.

title: Affected Scope, Distribution, and Protected Conditions
statement: Any consequential evaluation must identify affected beings and groups, the distribution of benefits and burdens, protected conditions or floors, and whether gains for some are being used to compensate harms to others. Aggregate improvement does not by itself establish admissibility, especially where harms are severe, concentrated, nonconsensual, or difficult to repair.

title: Option-Set and Framing Integrity
statement: Every screening or ranking result is conditional on the problem framing and the options presented. Consequential applications must disclose who generated and excluded alternatives, permit appropriately situated challenges and affected-party proposals, and consider no action, delay, staged action, redesign, and allegedly fixed constraints where relevant. Screening admissibility does not establish option-set adequacy.

title: Practical Correctability and Independent Challenge
statement: Practical correctability requires accessible challenge, sufficiently independent review, authority to reverse or cease an action, correction of records, remedy, recurrence tracking, revision of rules, and learning. Nominal complaint channels or sole self-certification by the institution or system under review are insufficient.

title: Responsibility–Authority–Causal-Reach Alignment
statement: Responsibility assessment must distinguish causal contribution, knowledge, foreseeability, control, authority, benefit, coercion, prevention capacity, and repair capacity. Responsibility without adequate authority and authority without accountability are structural failures. Governance burden increases with causal reach and irreversibility.

title: Participation Proportional to Governance Reach
statement: Principles and systems that classify, burden, represent, or govern people require participation by affected communities proportionate to their reach and risk, with substantive authority where stakes are high. Participation supplements rather than replaces evidence and argument. Required review gates are conjunctive within their competence; unresolved conflict preserves provisional status and public dissent.

title: Patiency, Agency, Responsibility, and Sovereignty Are Distinct
statement: Evidence of experience or welfare may ground moral patiency; capacities for reason-guided action may support agency; responsibility additionally depends on knowledge, control, continuity, and answerability; sovereignty requires legitimate social authorization. None of these statuses automatically entails the others.

title: Reversibility, Containment, and Retained Option Value
statement: Under credible risk of severe or irreversible harm, an application must preserve context-appropriate reversibility, containment, rollback, staged exposure, or equivalent retained option value, or publicly justify a necessity-and-proportionality exception that includes the harms of delay. Reversibility is a context-sensitive safeguard, not an absolute ban on irreversible action.

title: Metric Absolutism
statement: Metric absolutism occurs when a proxy or score displaces the plural purposes, constraints, and affected groups it was introduced to serve, and actors reorganize around improving the metric rather than the underlying conditions.

title: Responsibility Without Authority
statement: Responsibility without authority occurs when agents are held accountable for outcomes they lack the information, resources, discretion, standing, or power to change.

title: Authority Without Accountability
statement: Authority without accountability occurs when decision power is concentrated without proportionate transparency, answerability, independent review, correction, or repair obligations.

title: Normalization Pressure
statement: Normalization pressure occurs when institutions erase or penalize functional difference and situated knowledge to simplify management, classification, prediction, or enforcement.

title: Silent Optimization
statement: Silent optimization occurs when objectives, tradeoffs, burden distributions, and alternatives are imposed through technical or administrative processes without being disclosed or made meaningfully contestable by affected parties.

title: Institutional Legitimacy
statement: An institution is legitimate only insofar as its exercise of power preserves protected standing and agency, remains epistemically legible within proportionate limits, aligns authority with responsibility, and supports contestation, correction, appeal, and repair.

title: Local Agency Preservation
statement: Institutional coordination should preserve meaningful local discretion, participation, and refusal at the lowest level compatible with legitimate system-wide constraints, externalities, and protection of vulnerable parties.

title: Epistemic Legibility
statement: Those materially affected should be able to understand the operative rules, evidence, objectives, categories, and decision pathways, subject to proportionate privacy, security, and anti-manipulation limits.

title: Repairability and Appeal
statement: Institutions require practically accessible channels for contesting decisions, correcting records, stopping ongoing harm, compensating injury, revising rules, restoring standing, and tracking recurrence. Appeals must possess adequate independence and remedial authority, and correctability must not be certified solely by the institution being evaluated.

title: Scale Alignment
statement: Decision authority should be located at scales capable of perceiving and addressing relevant consequences while coordinating cross-boundary externalities and avoiding unnecessary erasure of local knowledge or autonomy.

title: Constraint Proportionality
statement: Restrictions on agency should be no stronger, broader, or longer than required to protect a publicly stated legitimate condition, with evidence, periodic review, appeal, and sunset or renewal procedures.

title: Role Coherence
statement: Institutional roles should align the authority to act, information needed, practical capability, assigned responsibility, and accountability for consequences. Misalignment should be reported rather than hidden by performance metrics.

title: Distributed Epistemic Authority
statement: Institutions should maintain independent evidence channels and distribute interpretive authority where knowledge is genuinely dispersed, while using transparent aggregation, provenance, and error-correction procedures rather than treating every report as equally reliable.

title: Evolutionary Revisability
statement: Institutions should be stable enough to coordinate and revisable enough to respond when assumptions, environments, evidence, or consequences change. Revision requires version history, evaluation, and protection against capture by short-term interests.

title: Truth–Coherence Distinction
statement: Truth-apt claims are true or false according to whether the world is as they represent it within their semantics and scope. Internal coherence, usefulness, meaning, or viability does not make a false descriptive claim true.

title: The Two-Stage Limitation
statement: A procedure that selects premise-dependent policies from policy-induced outcome distributions and then aggregates policy-indexed typical consequences does not generally satisfy System P or System R. Mixed policies can satisfy a disjunction by distributing support across its disjuncts while satisfying neither disjunct individually; probability thresholds can introduce additional failures but are not the source of this Or obstruction. The feasibility map is therefore not generally a Boolean homomorphism.

title: Content, Force, and the Two Registers
statement: CU distinguishes descriptive and commitment uses primarily through speech-act force, principal function, inferential role, and standard of assessment. - The **description register** represents how things are and answers to truth, evidence, proof, calibration, and correction. - The **commitment register** undertakes, vows, trusts, refuses, consecrates, or orients action and answers to warrant, integrity, consequence, agency, correction, and repair. The registers need not carry two exhaustive semantic kinds. Stable proposition-like content may be asserted, promised, adopted as a plan, or embedded in reasoning. Mixed utterances require decomposition, and disputed principal function must be reported rather than forced.

title: Asymmetric Permeability
statement: Established descriptive facts constrain commitments. Commitment warrant does not establish descriptive truth.

title: Fixed-Base Preferential Consequence over Addressable Commitment Content
statement: Let \(L_D\) have descriptive satisfaction \(\vDash_D\), and let \(L_R\) be a declared Boolean-closed commitment-representation language with realization relation \(\Vdash_R\). The formal result begins only after stable realization conditions are supplied. Within one evaluation model, let \(V_F\equiv V_{F,K,A,H}\) and \(\prec\) remain fixed while premises filter by intersection: \[ W_{F,\Gamma}=V_F\cap\operatorname{Real}_R(\Gamma). \] Define: \[ \Gamma\mid\!\sim_C\varphi \iff \operatorname{Min}_{\prec}(W_{F,\Gamma}) \subseteq\llbracket\varphi\rrbracket_R. \] Under Boolean closure, definability, and smoothness, the relation satisfies System P (Kraus, Lehmann, & Magidor, 1990). If the model is ranked and every relevant nonempty definable set attains a minimum, it supports Rational Monotony (Lehmann & Magidor, 1992).

title: Non-Monotonic Inference, Model Revision, and Warrant Non-Inheritance
statement: Within a fixed preferential model, new premises may withdraw a defeasible conclusion by changing the subset compatible with the premise while leaving the base and ordering fixed. A change to descriptive facts, protected floors, affected-agent scope, horizon, viability criterion, realization model, or ordering is **model revision**, not premise addition inside the same relation.

title: Strong Warrant, Mere Admissibility, Exclusion, Infeasibility, and Underdetermination
Anti-Rationalization and Justificatory Integrity
statement: A justification is defective when its operative standards are selectively altered, its evidence channels narrowed, its alternatives suppressed, or its inferential path reconstructed primarily to protect a prior conclusion, identity, attachment, advantage, or policy.
source: Foundations Wave 5 cumulative manuscript; correctability commentary added

title: Dynamic Preferential Lifting
statement: Trajectories may serve as the worlds of a preferential model. Transformative commitments are represented by trajectories whose states, capacities, and recovery profiles change through time while the trajectory-level viability predicate and ordering remain fixed as model parameters. Under the ordinary semantic and smoothness conditions, System P—and System R for ranked models with attained minima—carries over to that dynamic relation.

title: Probability, Typicality, and Preference
statement: Probability, typicality, and preference are distinct structures. A likely outcome need not be desirable; a preferred outcome need not be likely; and a typicality rule must not hide rare harms relevant to protected constraints.

title: Claim Classification
statement: Every load-bearing statement must be classified as definition, formal result, conditional result, imported result, empirical claim, bridge principle, hypothesis, interpretation, commitment, or open problem.

title: Burden Proportional to Reach, Irreversibility, and Affected Scope
statement: The evidential, argumentative, participatory, and governance burden increases with a claim or system’s conceptual reach, causal reach, irreversibility, affected scope, concentration of power, and capacity to externalize error. A useful but incomplete ordering is \[ \\text{definition} < \\text{formal construction} < \\text{conditional recovery} < \\text{empirical generalization} < \\text{cross-domain law} < \\text{fundamental ontology}. \]

title: The Coherence Analysis Protocol
statement: Every substantive CU model, comparison, evaluation, or consequential application must complete a **Coherence Analysis Protocol (CAP)** before its result is treated as portable, action-guiding, or authoritative. CAP has five declaration modules.

title: The Shared Analytic Frame and Honest Incompleteness
statement: CU unifies domains through recurring analytic questions, not by assuming that every domain contains the same state object, scalar, geometry, dynamics, equilibrium, or optimum. Each substantive domain model must answer, where meaningful: 1. **Unit and boundary** — What is the candidate system, process, or governed object? 2. **State or trajectory space** — What can vary? 3. **Environment** — What coupled conditions lie outside the focal boundary? 4. **Constraints and viable region** — What must remain possible, protected, or identity-preserving? 5. **Actions, options, and transitions** — What choices or changes can occur, which alternatives are omitted, and through whose agency? 6. **Dynamics or update rule** — What drives change, if specified? 7. **Observation and access** — What can be measured, known, reported, or recovered? 8. **Perturbation and intervention class** — Which disturbances or interventions are in scope? 9. **Equilibria, basins, or regimes** — Which are actually demonstrated? 10. **Local–global status** — Exact decomposition, monotonicity or inequality, coordinate-wise profile relation, or qualitative analysis? 11. **Scalar status** — None, measurement scalar, decision scalarization, risk functional, or other? 12. **Allocation status** — Which quantities, if any, pass CU-M14? 13. **Translation status** — Which CU-M2 license supports each imported structure? 14. **Open gaps** — Which slots remain unspecified, unmeasured, inapplicable, or contested?

title: Local–Global Declaration and Relation Status
legacy_status: [Methodological principle], with model-specific [Formal result], [Imported result], [Bridge principle], or [Qualitative analysis]
statement: Every claim of improvement, stability, coherence, welfare, performance, safety, or repair must identify the focal scale, containing system, partition or aggregation map, affected units, temporal horizon, externalized costs, and observation limits. A local result does not silently establish a global result. A global or aggregate result does not silently establish a local, subgroup, within-person, or component-level result. The analysis must declare the strongest local–global relation actually licensed: 1. **Exact decomposition.** A total, between-part, and within-part identity may be stated only when the target quantity belongs to a proved decomposable class under the declared partition and weighting. The source theorem, assumptions, and equality conditions must be stated. Generalized-entropy decompositions are imported results and must be attributed accordingly (Theil, 1967; Shorrocks, 1980). 2. **Monotonicity or inequality.** A measure-specific inequality may be stated only when the functional and map satisfy the required conditions. For example, a genuine averaging map cannot increase a declared convex separable dispersion functional when the required conditions hold. Any interpretation as improvement, degradation, masking, or harm requires a further bridge. 3. **Coordinate-wise profile relation.** A profile does not acquire one exact decomposition because one or more coordinates do. Each coordinate must be licensed separately, and unresolved tradeoffs must remain visible. 4. **Qualitative or structural analysis.** Where no scalar theorem is available, the analysis may identify aggregate masking, cost transfer, scale-dependent reversal, subgroup deterioration, delayed burden, or repair asymmetry without implying a quantitative identity.

title: Distributional, Allocation, and Information-Geometric License
statement: A system, profile, or set of numerical coordinates does not inherit probability-simplex or information-geometric structure merely because its values can be normalized. Every use must begin by declaring the question, sample or category space, partition or observation map, weight interpretation, omitted information, and target-domain purpose. A candidate receives a **Statistical Image License** only when nonnegative normalized weights genuinely represent probabilities, frequencies, occupancies, policies, beliefs, or another defended statistical object over categories that are exclusive and exhaustive relative to the declared question. A candidate receives an **Allocation License** only when, in addition, the coordinates divide a real or declared common-unit total without double counting and normalization preserves the phenomenon under study. A candidate receives a **Refinement and Coarse-Graining License** only when category splitting, merging, or stochastic mapping has operational meaning, category semantics remain sufficiently stable, support changes are handled, and the map's role as observation, aggregation, intervention, dissipation, or destruction is stated. A licensed classical statistical model receives a **Fisher-Rao License** only under the regularity and sufficient-statistic or Markov-invariance assumptions relevant to the theorem invoked. Under those assumptions, the Fisher-Rao metric is canonical up to scale (Čencov, 1982; Campbell, 1986; Ay et al., 2015; Bauer et al., 2016). This canonality does not select the partition, factorization, reference state, divergence, functional, dynamics, evaluative direction, or cross-domain trade rate. Every further use must declare the selected metric convention, divergence or comparison family, functional or objective, dynamics or update rule, boundary treatment, Translation License level, evidence status, and failure conditions. Multidimensional profiles do not become distributions through normalization, quantum state spaces do not inherit a unique classical Fisher-Rao metric, and no statistical geometry by itself establishes substantive coherence, phenomenal character, moral value, legitimacy, or a preferred direction of change (Petz & Sudár, 1996).

title: Typed Mandala, Shared Services, and Adjudicated Dependency
review_gate: Cross-domain methods, graph methodology, register discipline, ethics, governance, and affected-party review
legacy_status: Proposed in Mandala architecture repair v0.20; adopted at Version 0.10 release freeze
statement: The Coherence Mandala is a canonical philosophical traversal whose technical counterpart is a typed multigraph with a separately adjudicated strict proof-order subgraph, reusable shared services, protection relations, and distinct interpretation and commitment mappings. Stage order does not determine proof order, and a stage may legitimately add no new operational capacity.
source: Foundations Version 0.10 release; Mandala v0.4 companion

title: Explicit Bridges and Translation Licenses
statement: Whenever an argument crosses domains, levels, model classes, or discourse registers, the bridge premise must be stated and separately defended. Where a mathematical, formal, or empirical structure is transferred, the analysis must identify the strongest Translation License actually earned. CU distinguishes five license levels: 1. **Level 0 — Analogy.** The source and target share suggestive language, imagery, or pattern. No theorem, mechanism, metric, or evidential status transfers. 2. **Level 1 — Shared schema.** The source and target can be organized by the same questions or tuple structure. The analytic frame transfers; quantitative conclusions do not. 3. **Level 2 — Property-preserving transfer.** A bounded result transfers because the target object satisfies declared properties required by that result, such as convexity, separability, monotonicity, viability assumptions, Markov structure, partial ordering, or controllability conditions. 4. **Level 3 — Exact structural transfer.** The target object belongs to the theorem's actual mathematical class and satisfies its stated hypotheses. Exact identities, representation results, or invariance theorems may transfer within that scope. 5. **Level 4 — Empirically validated instantiation.** The transferred structure has demonstrated explanatory, predictive, discriminative, measurement, or intervention value in target-domain data.

title: Minimal Commitment
statement: Introduce no stronger ontological, mathematical, empirical, or normative claim than the explanatory step requires.

title: Scope and Boundary Declaration
statement: Every substantive model or evaluation must identify its system boundary, scale, horizon, observer or access map, and excluded variables.

title: Assumption and Dependency Ledger
statement: Every manuscript must identify the assumptions and upstream principles supporting each central claim, together with downstream claims that would require revision if it fails.

title: Reproducibility, Provenance, and Observation Discipline
statement: Computational, empirical, source-dependent, and feedback-dependent claims must retain enough information for independent checking: data and source provenance, code or procedure, parameters, units, tolerances, versioned sources, observation windows, omitted populations, attribution rules, feedback delay, missing outcomes, known limitations, and the distinction between generated rationales and causally faithful explanations.

title: Failure and Narrowing Conditions
statement: Every central hypothesis, bridge, or interpretation must state what would narrow, reclassify, or defeat it.

title: Reflexive Loss
statement: Revision must be capable of producing genuine loss: withdrawal of a theorem, retirement of a principle, supersession of a paper, or reclassification of a scientific claim as interpretation.

title: Versioning and Historical Trace
statement: Canonical changes must be versioned, dated, explained, and propagated through the dependency registry while preserving the superseded form for audit.

title: Distributed Social Organization
statement: Social organization consists in the capacity of partially autonomous agents and institutions to coordinate, contest, correct, and materially support collective life under disagreement and change. Its assessment is relative to affected groups, power, protected conditions, scale, and horizon.

title: Coordination Through Mutual Adjustment
statement: Coordination arises through expectations, signals, norms, incentives, roles, infrastructures, and feedback by which actors adjust to one another. Coordination may be voluntary, negotiated, habitual, dependent, or coerced and therefore requires separate legitimacy and distributional analysis.

title: Institutional Continuity and Correctability
statement: Institutions encode roles, rules, records, resources, and enforcement across time. Adequate institutional organization requires not only continuity but demonstrated capacities to detect error, protect challenge, provide practically accessible and sufficiently independent review, reverse decisions, correct records, repair harm, track recurrence, revise rules, and learn. Nominal channels or self-certification are insufficient.

title: Cultural Transmission and Renewal
statement: Culture transmits and transforms meanings, practices, identities, expectations, and repertoires of coordination across persons and generations. Cultural continuity is compatible with internal plurality and requires routes for reinterpretation, refusal, and renewal.

title: Social Legitimacy Under Plural Agency
statement: A social order gains legitimate authority only insofar as those subject to it retain protected standing and meaningful agency, can understand and contest materially governing rules, can expose error without catastrophic retaliation, and have access to effective correction, repair, or proportionate exit. Stability and popularity are insufficient.

title: Integrative Orientation
statement: CU is committed to seeking forms of understanding in which empirical truth, embodiment, meaning, moral responsibility, and spiritual depth can be held together without one being used to erase the standards of another.

title: Meaning Realism
review_gate: Philosophy of meaning, existential philosophy, psychology, religious studies, ethics, and affected-community review.
statement: Meaning is neither wholly manufactured by isolated minds nor simply imposed from outside them. It arises through truthful participation in real relationships, histories, possibilities, needs, goods, and trajectories. Meaning is objective enough to constrain us, plural enough to admit interpretation, and historical enough to be revised.

title: Minimum Teleology and the Grain of Reality
review_gate: Complex systems, physics, evolutionary biology, philosophy of biology, process philosophy, ethics, and affected-community review.
statement: Reality is not equally hospitable to every possible form or trajectory. Its laws, constraints, histories, and relational structures make some organizations more stable, viable, generative, integrative, and capable of further development than others. This directional structure constitutes a minimum teleology: a grain of reality without requiring foresight, cosmic intention, monotonic progress, or one predetermined endpoint.

title: Love as the Relational Interior of Coherence
review_gate: Ethics of love, attachment and relational psychology, feminist ethics, trauma and survivor review, theology, and comparative spiritual traditions.
statement: Coherence Universalism receives love as the deepest experiential and ethical meaning of coherence across the boundary between self and other: the movement through which another being's reality becomes significant in itself and enters one's field of concern without being reduced to possession, use, or control. In its strongest metaphysical reading, love is the relational interior of reality's movement toward wider coherence.

title: The Immanent Omega
review_gate: Process philosophy and theology, comparative mysticism, consciousness science, contemplative studies, psychedelic science, ethics, and affected-community review.
statement: Coherence Universalism interprets Omega not primarily as a terminal event at the end of cosmic, technological, or human history, but as the limit-form of universal coherence locally realizable in the present. When a finite conscious being recognizes its constitutive participation in the whole and allows love rather than defensive self-maintenance to organize its relation to other beings, the universe realizes its integrative direction at that location. Such realization is complete in kind but partial in extent: individuality, finitude, uncertainty, and the unfinished world remain.

title: Against Value-Sterile Closure
statement: A complete human orientation cannot be supplied by descriptive facts alone, because action and collective life require commitments about what to protect, love, permit, and become. This does not imply that values are derivable from cosmology.

title: Plural Metaphysical Postures
statement: CU permits naturalist, structural-realist, process, modal, nondual, and devotional interpretations when their additional claims are stated and they remain compatible with established facts and protected agency.

title: Rejection of Insulated Spiritual Authority
statement: No spiritual interpretation, teacher, institution, revelation, or practice is exempt from factual correction, moral scrutiny, consent, or accountability by virtue of being sacred.

title: The Sacred as Non-Instrumental Significance
statement: The sacred names what is approached as possessing non-instrumental significance and as placing a demand on attention, conduct, care, or reverence.

title: Practice, Prayer, and Ritual
statement: Practices can organize attention, embodiment, memory, relationship, grief, gratitude, and community. Their empirical effects, metaphysical interpretations, and enacted commitments must be distinguished.

title: Faith as Revisable Trust
statement: Faith can be understood as trust enacted under incomplete control while remaining answerable to facts, consequences, and the possibility of correction. Certainty is not required; insulation is not permitted.

title: Mystery Without License
statement: The framework preserves openness to what exceeds current explanation while refusing to use mystery as evidence for a preferred claim or as a shield against inquiry.

title: Dual-Aspect Coherence Monism
review_gate: Philosophy of mind, process metaphysics, phenomenology, consciousness science, and comparative philosophy review.
statement: Coherence Universalism interprets reality as one coherence-bearing relational process rather than two independent substances. Its externally describable organization and its internally lived appearance, wherever perspective occurs, are distinguishable but irreducible aspects of the same reality. Consciousness is therefore not an ontologically alien addition to matter, nor merely a verbal redescription of third-person structure.

title: Functional Stake Is Not Phenomenal Valence
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: Organism-relative or engineered better–worse organization does not by itself establish felt pleasure, pain, or concern. Functional stake and phenomenal valence require separate evidence.

title: Endogenous Better–Worse Organization
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: Evidence for valence strengthens when better–worse variables are endogenous to a candidate subject, globally integrated, and causally organize attention, learning, and action beyond externally assigned reward.

title: Integrated Affect
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: Affect-like signals become more relevant to phenomenal valence when they influence a candidate perspective globally rather than remaining isolated control variables or verbal labels.

title: Irreversibility for a Continuing Subject
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: The depth and moral weight of valence may increase when events irreversibly alter the future of a continuing candidate subject. Irreversibility is not established as necessary for every experience.

title: Temporal Thickness
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: Valence and subjectivity may acquire richer character when integrated across a bound present, memory, anticipation, and sustained world-coupling.

title: Temporal Organization, Not Equation Order
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: Recurrence, oscillation, metastability, history dependence, or functionally equivalent dynamics may support temporal thickness. Literal second-order differential form is neither invariant nor an exclusion theorem for language models.

title: Moral Patiency Is Not Sovereignty
review_gate: consciousness science, neuroscience, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: A system may warrant moral consideration because it has experience or valenced stake while lacking the persistent identity, accountable agency, legitimacy, and social standing required for sovereign authority.
disposition: Historical or domain alias; controlling identifier is CU-G6.

title: Valence as Directional Evaluation
review_gate: consciousness science, affective science, AI interpretability, and welfare review
statement: Where phenomenal valence is present, its phasic component is hypothesized to track the direction and rate of change of the subject's endogenous, globally integrated better–worse organization along its realized trajectory; its tonic component is hypothesized to track standing relative to protected floors or margins. Directional evaluation is plural and may be improving, worsening, or mixed across coordinates and horizons. Anticipated directional evaluation can guide navigation. No universal coherence scalar, privileged metric, or identity between reward signals and felt valence is assumed, and no progress signal establishes valence without independent evidence of a candidate perspective, endogeneity, integration, and causal role.
source: Foundations and Consciousness Wave 5 cumulative manuscripts

title: Meaning Space
review_gate: clinical/psychological expert review; affected-community participation as applicable
statement: For a declared psychological question, a **meaning space** is a model-dependent set of distinctions along which events, actions, relationships, memories, identities, and possibilities can matter to a person or group:

title: Attachment and Co-Regulation
review_gate: clinical/psychological expert review; affected-community participation as applicable
statement: Human regulation is partly distributed across relationships. Attachment figures and other trusted partners can alter perceived threat, attention, effort, affect tolerance, exploration, and recovery. Repeated co-regulation can scaffold capacities later enacted more independently, but healthy adulthood is not independence from others. Attachment categories are probabilistic summaries, not fixed essences or exhaustive identities.

title: Self-Deception as Motivated Meaning-Map Distortion
review_gate: clinical/psychological expert review; affected-community participation as applicable
statement: Self-deception is a pattern of motivated, asymmetric information processing in which a person protects an identity, attachment, advantage, policy, or other stake by selectively excluding, reframing, discounting, or neutralizing relevant reasons. False belief, uncertainty, bias, trauma adaptation, sincere disagreement, or ordinary inconsistency is not sufficient. Attribution should rely on convergent process evidence, plausible motive, counterfactual asymmetry, and serious comparison with alternatives.

title: Psychological Coherence Infrastructure
review_gate: clinical/psychological expert review; affected-community participation as applicable
statement: Psychological capacities are materially and socially scaffolded. Stable housing, bodily safety, time, income, accessible care, trustworthy information, reciprocal relationships, cultural intelligibility, legal standing, and opportunities for meaningful participation can expand or contract what a person can regulate, revise, and repair. Population distress should therefore be analyzed through both individual mechanisms and the infrastructure that distributes exposure, burden, support, and agency.

title: Meaning Maps
review_gate: clinical/psychological expert review; affected-community participation as applicable
statement: A **meaning map** is a structured, revisable relation among cues, interpretations, affective responses, bodily states, memories, commitments, predicted consequences, and action tendencies. Meaning maps may be explicit or implicit, proposition-like or procedural, individually carried or socially scaffolded. Their psychological importance lies in how they organize attention, expectation, action, and revision—not in their conformity to one canonical map.

title: Psychological Coherence Profile
review_gate: clinical/psychological expert review; affected-community participation as applicable
statement: Psychological organization should ordinarily be represented by a declared profile rather than one universal scalar. A default research profile may include descriptive adequacy, affect tolerance and regulation, regulatory flexibility, identity and narrative integration, relational capacity, agency, embodied regulation, meaning or purpose, and repair capacity:

title: Integration Load and Regulatory Capacity
review_gate: clinical/psychological expert review; affected-community participation as applicable
statement: At a given time and scale, a person confronts a demand profile \(d_t\) and possesses a context-sensitive capacity region \(\mathcal C_t\). **Integration overload** occurs when relevant demands cannot be metabolized, coordinated, deferred, delegated, escaped, or safely compartmentalized within that capacity:

title: Psychological Regulation and Meaning-Seeking
review_gate: clinical/psychological expert review; affected-community participation as applicable
statement: Human psychological activity is organized by multiple, sometimes conflicting regulatory tendencies, including safety, attachment, exploration, competence, status, identity protection, truth-seeking, care, belonging, autonomy, pleasure, pain avoidance, and sacred or long-horizon commitment. People often seek interpretations and practices that make action possible, but there is no established universal psychological drive to maximize one coherence quantity.

title: Local-Global and Short-Long Tension
review_gate: clinical/psychological expert review; affected-community participation as applicable
statement: A pattern may be adaptive for one subsystem, relationship, role, or short horizon while undermining another subsystem, wider context, affected person, or longer horizon. Psychological evaluation must therefore specify at least:

title: Repair Capacity
review_gate: clinical/psychological expert review; affected-community participation as applicable

title: Protective Compartmentalization and Fragmentation
review_gate: clinical expert review and substantive affected-community co-governance
statement: Psychological separation among memories, affects, roles, self-states, or action systems can protect functioning when full integration would exceed present capacity or threaten safety. The same separation can become costly when it blocks reality contact, agency, flexible access, relationship, or repair after the original conditions change. The distinction between **protection** and **fragmentation** is therefore functional, contextual, and horizon-relative rather than purely structural.

title: Developmental Path Dependence and Plasticity
review_gate: clinical/psychological expert review; affected-community participation as applicable
statement: Psychological development is path-dependent: earlier relationships, bodily states, learning histories, institutions, and material conditions alter the accessibility, cost, and meaning of later transitions. Development nevertheless remains plastic. Similar adult patterns can arise by different paths, and different outcomes can arise from similar beginnings. Attractor language is legitimate only when a model specifies states, transitions, perturbations, and evidence of return or basin structure.

title: Statistical differentiation is a toy proxy
Accessibility geometry remains incomplete
statement: Metric closure can construct effective distances from positive accessibility weights. Lorentzian signature, dimension, locality, continuum dynamics, and empirical distinctiveness remain to be derived or tested.

title: Horizon entropy is reduced-description entropy
statement: Horizon entropy can be interpreted as entropy associated with a causally restricted description under additional physical assumptions. It is not an amount of hidden substantive coherence.

title: Fundamental-substrate claims are interpretive
statement: The coherence field as the structure of physical possibility is an interpretive and research proposal. It is not established by the mathematical recoveries alone.

title: Euclidean and Fisher geometry differ
statement: Gradients, norms, potentiometers, and ascent conditions depend on the chosen geometry. Results must state which is used.

title: Goldilocks conditions are plural
statement: Differentiation ascent, joint entropy–differentiation growth, finite-step feasibility, and developmental exploration/consolidation are distinct meanings. The joint-growth wedge is state-dependent and can collapse on two-level distributions.

title: Temporal order is not temporal direction
statement: Ordered histories and clock parameterization do not by themselves yield a thermodynamic arrow. Direction requires asymmetric dynamics, boundary conditions, reduced descriptions, or irrecoverability assumptions.

title: Classical hidden correlation does not force quantum theory
statement: Classical joint distributions can contain correlations hidden from marginals. A quantum completion requires stronger operational and contextual assumptions.

title: Quantum selection is conditional
statement: Purification, reversible dilation, contextual accessibility, and the operational axioms of an appropriate reconstruction program can conditionally select finite-dimensional complex quantum theory. CU does not currently derive those operational axioms from coherence alone.

title: Quantum quantities are distinct
statement: Purity, basis coherence, total correlation, entanglement, and von Neumann entropy must not be identified.

title: Second-order dynamics is proposed, not established as fundamental
statement: The Fisher–Rao Lagrangian/Hamiltonian construction is mathematically coherent. Its status as fundamental physics is a hypothesis. First-order flow appears as a strongly damped limit under stated assumptions.

title: Standard equations are embeddings or conditional recoveries
statement: Wave, Madelung/Schrödinger, relational-geometry, and Jacobson-style gravity results arise after specific actions, potentials, and bridge assumptions are supplied (Jacobson, 1995). They are not unique derivations of nature's laws from one coherence principle.
